clue.text: Have body of policemen forward of vessel

indicators.note: forward of puts the first piece in front of the second in the charade

parts.note: a posse is a band of men gathered by a sheriff to keep the law
SS stands for steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: An order to take command of a squad of officers ahead of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is a straightforward synonym of having it.

clue.text: Most of his darts hit the bull

definitions.text: Most of his darts hit the bull

parts.words: Most of his darts hit the bull
parts.note: not a darts player hitting the bullseye but a mounted bullfighter whose lances strike the animal

explanation.surface: A darts player who keeps scoring bullseyes.
explanation.definitionFit: In bullfighting the horseman who goads the bull with a lance is a mounted lancer.

parts.note: a sensation is a feeling
a ship heels when it leans over, or lists

explanation.surface: A gossip who enjoys the feel of a heel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabloid writer who exaggerates for effect is someone who peddles scandal.

clue.text: Last of the old line of trees

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the LMS, London Midland and Scottish Railway, was a British railway company before nationalisation in 1948

explanation.surface: The last surviving row of trees from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old line' is a railway line here, not a row of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Deciduous hardwood trees of the genus Ulmus.

clue.text: To be in saddle at high speed makes a lump on horse's back

parts.note: to sit is to be in the saddle on a horse
fast means quickly

explanation.surface: Riding hard in the saddle gives a horse a sore on its back.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard swelling on a horse's back caused by saddle rubbing is this equine complaint.

definitions.meaning: an office is a task or obligation one must perform
customs are the charges levied on imported goods

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a moral obligation (an office) and the import levy collected by customs officers.

parts.note: to shadow someone is to follow, or dog, them
pitch is tar

explanation.surface: A star throwing shadows across a sports field.
explanation.definitionFit: The brightest star in the night sky lies in Canis Major.

clue.text: Gin-but not all of it, overturned

indicators.note: overturned says the word for a portion is turned the other way, reading backwards in this down clue

parts.note: a part is not the whole

explanation.surface: A glass of gin knocked over before it was finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin' is the snare, not the spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a snare for catching animals.

definitions.meaning: a sweet fruit drink, often diluted

explanation.definitionFit: The word means warmly amiable, and also names a sweet fruit drink or liqueur.

parts.note: not decorating with wallpaper but a lamp made of paper that hangs up

explanation.surface: Putting up wallpaper as a light job.
explanation.definitionFit: A collapsible paper lamp traditional in East Asia that is hung up for illumination.

clue.text: Movie-maker positions grip on the camera

indicators.note: positions is a verb here, arranging these letters in new places

explanation.surface: A film director places a hand firmly on the camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'positions' rearranges all fifteen letters of GRIP ON THE CAMERA; 'grip' looks like the film crew's gaffer job, which suits the misleading picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who directs photography on a film is a central figure in making the movie.

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the word for the poet is read backwards

parts.note: a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: An apartment set aside for a poet who has stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat in the sense of dull and lifeless matches a dreary, colourless quality.

definitions.meaning: a Cornish ... is a pastry case of meat and vegetables, the classic dish of Cornwall in south-west England

explanation.definitionFit: The word means pallid in complexion, and is also the folded meat-filled pastry for which Cornwall is famous.

clue.text: One who is opposed to a tin-opener

indicators.note: an opener breaks into a tin, so the letters of the phrase are broken up and reworked

explanation.surface: Someone who objects to using a can-opener.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word names a person against something, an opponent.

parts.note: not whisky or gin but the magical being of Arabian tales trapped in a lamp or bottle

explanation.surface: Whisky or gin sold in bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: A jinn of Arabian folklore, often pictured confined in a lamp or bottle.

parts.note: Offa, an 8th-century king of Mercia, built Offa's Dyke along the Welsh border

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone building an embankment left their junk behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste or refuse, from the entrails and scraps cut from a carcass.

clue.text: The purpose, in Split, is to get something to wear

indicators.note: in places the purpose inside the split

parts.note: a rent is a split or tear
an aim is a purpose

explanation.surface: A question of what one intends to do in the Croatian city of Split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' looks like the Croatian port, capitalised to mislead; it is a tear, RENT, which 'in' puts around AIM.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a literary term for clothing or garments.

parts.note: not the racket sport but the Badminton horse trials in Gloucestershire, where a horse may balk at a fence and decline to jump it

explanation.surface: A shuttlecock being hit back in a game of badminton.
explanation.walkthrough: Badminton Horse Trials is a famous English equestrian event; a horse stopping at a fence is penalised.
explanation.definitionFit: A rejection or knockback is a declining, as when a horse balks at a jump.

indicators.note: with joins the second piece after the first

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
firm means fixed solidly, as if cemented

explanation.surface: A description of reading about a wall support set in cement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buttress' is a verb here, to support or corroborate.
explanation.definitionFit: To corroborate a claim is to strengthen or support it, as a buttress supports a wall.

clue.text: Small dog takes the continental soup

parts.note: a chow is a breed of dog
der is German for the

explanation.surface: A little dog helping itself to some European soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick chunky soup of fish or clams.

definitions.meaning: the planet closest to the Sun
quicksilver, the liquid metal that slips through the fingers

explanation.definitionFit: It is the innermost planet, and the liquid metal whose beads are notoriously elusive to the touch.

clue.text: From the French, a blissful wine!

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A delightful drink that comes from France.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry white Burgundy produced around a town in the Yonne department.

parts.note: not a performer bowing to applause but a seated musician who picks up a bow to play

explanation.surface: A seated performer acknowledging applause.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the large stringed instrument sits and plays with a bow.

definitions.meaning: a Dalmatian dog has a white coat covered in dark spots

explanation.definitionFit: The word means picked out by sight, and also marked with dots like a Dalmatian's coat.

indicators.note: running suggests the letters are set in motion and moved about

explanation.surface: Car horns sounding as traffic crawls along.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds that hoot at night are a whimsical way of describing these nocturnal raptors.

clue.text: Make holes in linen or cotton

definitions.meaning: to bore through something with a rotating tool
a strong twilled fabric of linen or cotton

explanation.definitionFit: The word means boring with a bit, and is also a hard-wearing twilled textile.

clue.text: A French firm is a strange thing in Scotland

parts.note: un is the French for a
Co is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A French company being an odd sight north of the border.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots dialect uses the word as a noun for something odd or unusual.

definitions.meaning: a set of rooms forming a home, an apartment

explanation.definitionFit: The word means dull and monotonous, and is the British term for an apartment.

clue.text: Blue dye obtained from a duck-egg

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, nil, so called because a zero looks like a duck's egg

explanation.surface: A colouring made from the shell of a duck's egg.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a score of zero; 'duck-egg' blue is also a pale colour, which feeds the misleading picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo dye from a West Indian shrub.

clue.text: I, seldom in sunlit position, have my eyes opened in it

definitions.text: have my eyes opened in it

indicators.note: position as a verb means to arrange, so these letters are placed in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone rarely out in the sun has their eyes opened by it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being freed from false beliefs is the condition in which one's eyes are opened to the truth.

definitions.meaning: to tarry is to linger or remain
a rope supporting a ship's mast

explanation.definitionFit: The word means remain or linger, and is also a supporting rope or wire in a ship's rigging.

clue.text: Having hooked fingers, dealt no trick

indicators.note: a trick is a deception, so the letters play false and come out rearranged

explanation.surface: A card player making no deal and taking no trick.
explanation.walkthrough: The card-game surface of 'dealt' and 'trick' hides an anagram of DEALT NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Claws on a bird of prey are hooked digits, so a creature equipped with them is described this way.
